figures.finding: Monaco levies no income tax on individuals domiciled there; French nationals who moved to Monaco (or cannot show five years' habitual residence at 13 October 1962) stay taxable in France on all their income under article 7-1 of the 1963 Franco-Monegasque convention. The direct taxes (the land tax, the personal and furniture tax and the business licence tax) were abolished by Sovereign Ordinance of 8 February 1869.

exception.who: French nationals domiciled in Monaco (convention of 18 May 1963, art. 7-1)

value.abolishedBy: Ordonnance souveraine du 8 février 1869 (Journal de Monaco n° 556, 14 février 1869)

sources.said: A partir de ce jour sont supprimés dans Notre Principauté la Contribution foncière, la Contribution personnelle et mobilière et l'impôt des patentes. … Donné en Notre Palais à Monaco, le huit février mil huit cent soixante-neuf.

La principauté de Monaco ne soumet pas les personnes physiques qui ont leur domicile sur son territoire à l’impôt sur le revenu. Cela étant, l'article 7-1 de la convention fiscale entre la France et la principauté de Monaco signée à Paris le 18 mai 1963 prévoit, sous certaines conditions, de soumettre les ressortissants français domiciliés à Monaco à l’impôt sur le revenu en France à raison de l’ensemble de leurs revenus
En effet, Monaco ne connaissant ni impôt sur le revenu, ni impôt sur la fortune

figures.finding: From 1 October 2026 pay bears: CCSS (health and family, employer) 13.40% (13.45% where affiliated to the CGCS) up to EUR 10,000 a month; CAR pension 6.85% employee and 7.45% employer base plus 0.94% variable employer, up to EUR 6,276 a month; CMRC supplementary pension tranche A 10.020% (4.008% employee, 6.012% employer) up to EUR 4,067 and tranche B 24.290% (9.716%/14.574%) up to 8 times that; UNEDIC unemployment 6.40% (2.40%/4.00%) up to EUR 16,020 a month.
figures.applies: Salaried employees of Monaco employers; self-employed schemes (CAMTI/CARTI) were not read.

figures.finding: A Monaco freelancer's fee bears VAT levied on the same basis and at the same rates as in France (20% standard); the threshold therefore follows France.
figures.applies: Business transactions in Monaco (customs union with France, convention of 18 May 1963).

sources.said: Value Added Tax is levied on the same basis and at the same rate as in France. The most commonly applied rates are: The usual rate of 20% The reduced rate of 10%, except for basic products (5.5 %)

figures.finding: With no income tax there is nothing withheld from pay in Monaco but the social contributions; French nationals caught by article 7-1 follow France.
